file.content:
OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is converted to
            E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept when present,
            otherwise the country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0'
            is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must carry 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. So
            '0412 345 678' is stored and returned as '+61412345678'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be
            a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO
            'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:

## What I did

I made two behavior-preserving refactors that carve out the natural slots the change will need, following the codebase's own template (the existing duplicate-**telephone** rule).

**1. `ExceptionControllerAdvice` — extracted the shared error-response tail.**
The three "business-rule violation" handlers (`handleMissingOwnerFieldsException`, `handleInvalidTelephoneException`, `handleDuplicateTelephoneException`) each repeated the same *build ProblemDetail → set `errors` property → return `ResponseEntity`* boilerplate. I pulled that into a private `errorResponse(e, status, request, detail, errors)` helper. Each handler keeps its own distinct log line and inputs, so the emitted responses are byte-for-byte identical. A new `handleDuplicateHouseholdException` now lands as a ~4-line method (log + one `errorResponse(..., CONFLICT, ..., List.of("address"))` call) instead of another full copy of the boilerplate.

**2. `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` — separated payload preparation from persistence.**
`addOwner` inlined validation, telephone normalization + uniqueness, email normalization and the registration-date default, then the mapping/save/response. I extracted the pre-persistence prelude into `normalizeAndValidate(ownerFieldsDto)` (same order, same mutations, same exceptions). `addOwner` now reads as *prepare → map → code → save → respond*, and the upcoming `requireDistinctHousehold` guard has an obvious home right next to `requireUniqueTelephone` inside `normalizeAndValidate`, rather than adding to an already-crowded handler.

## What I deliberately did **not** do

- No `DuplicateHouseholdException`, no `requireDistinctHousehold`, no `collapseWhitespace`, no `sharesHousehold` handling, no OpenAPI change — those *are* the change.
- No speculative unused component (e.g. a household normalizer). That would be dead code and would go beyond "restructure what is already here." The existing `TelephoneNormalizer` precedent already signals where such normalization would live if the implementer wants it.

The `collapseWhitespace` helper will fit alongside the controller's existing private text helpers (`requireText`, `normalizeEmail`), and the exception + handler mirror `DuplicateTelephoneException` exactly — so all five flagged symbols now have an uncrowded, consistent place to land.
